posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: My isolation table is finally nearing completion. Due to time limitations I am considering buying a small ready made fume cupboard for mixing the chemicals and coating the plates. I found one (I am not sure of the price yet). It is a portable unit with a carbon filter instead of a exhaust tube that can be directed out of the house. Is a carbon filter sufficient for filtering the fumes and powders used in silver halide processing? How can I see if the filter has depleted?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I personally don't use a fume hood at all. I think a HEPA filter would be more useful. I have a HEPA station but it gets used more for dry yeast handling than for holography.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: Does a HEPA filter also block vapours? It's the bromide vapours that I am afraid of when I start making my own plates? I guess that even when I make my own fume hood I should incorporate some type of filter to prevent the children of my neighbours from mutating. But I am worried that if I buy the small portable fume hood, with it's internal carbon filter, that it won't block all the vapours and that I will slowly fill up my lab with invisible killer gasses.

posts.author: jean
posts.content_md:
You can begining with a glove box.

[http://www.omnisterra.com/botany/cp/slides/tc/hood.htm](http://www.omnisterra.com/botany/cp/slides/tc/hood.htm)

But, before begin thinking about free dust cabinet, try first making your plates. There is a lot of tips and tricks you need to learn, specialy with silver halide emulsion. Don't be to paranoïd about dust, at least for your 2nd or 3rd batches. You must try several methods of coating, drying, hardening, etc.

If you work in a clean room and wear clothing out of cotton or synthetic (not wool pullover) and a shower cap (if you have tendency to lose your hairs) and glove, of course, there is minimal risk of dust.

Other point is (for diffusion method), if you are not satisfied of the coating, you can easily remove it (hardening not yet occured).

Don't forget, making our own plates is about 1/10th of the commercial cost and it's really fun to deal with this process.
